questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A metallic circular loop is placed with its plane perpendicular to a uniform magnetic field of 0.3 T. If the radius of the loop decreases at a constant rate of $2\ mm\ s^{-1}$, what will be the induced emf in the loop, when the radius of the loop becomes 5 cm.
questions.solution:
Magnetic flux through the loop is given by $\Phi = BA = B\pi r^2$

According to Faraday's law of induction, the magnitude of the induced emf is:

$|e| = \left| \dfrac{d\Phi}{dt} \right| = B \cdot 2\pi r \left| \dfrac{dr}{dt} \right|$

Given:

$B = 0.3\ T$

$r = 5\ cm = 5 \times 10^{-2}\ m$

$\left| \dfrac{dr}{dt} \right| = 2\ mm\ s^{-1} = 2 \times 10^{-3}\ m\ s^{-1}$

Substituting the values:

$|e| = 0.3 \times 2\pi \times (5 \times 10^{-2}) \times (2 \times 10^{-3})$

$|e| = 0.3 \times 20\pi \times 10^{-5} = 6\pi \times 10^{-5}\ V$

$|e| = 6 \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 10^{-5} \approx 18.857 \times 10^{-5}\ V$

$|e| \approx 1.89 \times 10^{-4}\ V$

Answer: $1.89 \times 10^{-4}\ V$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A square loop of wire 2.2 cm on each side contains 2 turns and has a total resistance of $0.0002\ \Omega$. It is located 22 cm from a long straight current carrying wire. If the current in the straight wire is increased at a steady rate from 20 A to 50 A in 5 s, determine the magnitude of the current induced in the squared loop.
questions.solution:
Given:
Side of the square loop, $a = 2.2 \text{ cm} = 0.022 \text{ m}$
Number of turns, $N = 2$
Total resistance, $R = 0.0002\ \Omega$
Distance from the straight wire, $d = 22 \text{ cm} = 0.22 \text{ m}$
Rate of change of current, $\dfrac{dI}{dt} = \dfrac{50 - 20}{5} = 6 \text{ A/s}$

Since the size of the loop is small compared to its distance from the wire ($a \ll d$), we can assume the magnetic field is approximately uniform over the area of the loop and equal to the field at its center.
The magnetic field at distance $d$ is:
$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi d}$

The total magnetic flux linked with the $N$ turns of the loop is:
$\Phi = N B A = N \left( \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2\pi d} \right) a^2$

According to Faraday's law of induction, the induced emf is:
$\mathcal{E} = \dfrac{d\Phi}{dt} = \dfrac{N \mu_0 a^2}{2\pi d} \dfrac{dI}{dt}$

The induced current in the loop is:
$i = \dfrac{\mathcal{E}}{R} = \dfrac{N \mu_0 a^2}{2\pi d R} \dfrac{dI}{dt}$

Substituting the given values:
$i = \dfrac{2 \times (4\pi \times 10^{-7}) \times (0.022)^2}{2\pi \times 0.22 \times 0.0002} \times 6$

$i = \dfrac{4 \times 10^{-7} \times 0.000484}{0.000044} \times 6$

$i = \dfrac{1.936 \times 10^{-10}}{4.4 \times 10^{-5}} \times 6$

$i = 4.4 \times 10^{-6} \times 6 = 26.4 \times 10^{-6} \text{ A}$

$i = 0.0264 \text{ mA}$

Rounding to two significant figures, the induced current is approximately $0.026 \text{ mA}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A circular coil of radius 7 cm and 40 turns is rotated about its vertical diameter with an angular speed of 40 radians per second in a uniform horizontal magnetic field of $4 \times 10^{-2}\ T$. What is the maximum current induced in the coil if the resistance of the coil is $11\ \Omega$?
questions.solution:
Given:
Number of turns, $N = 40$
Radius of the coil, $r = 7\ \text{cm} = 0.07\ \text{m}$
Angular speed, $\omega = 40\ \text{rad/s}$
Magnetic field, $B = 4 \times 10^{-2}\ \text{T}$
Resistance, $R = 11\ \Omega$

The maximum induced emf in the coil is given by:
$\varepsilon_{max} = N B A \omega$

Substituting the area $A = \pi r^2$:
$\varepsilon_{max} = 40 \times (4 \times 10^{-2}) \times \left(\dfrac{22}{7} \times (0.07)^2\right) \times 40$

$\varepsilon_{max} = 1600 \times 4 \times 10^{-2} \times \dfrac{22}{7} \times 49 \times 10^{-4}$

$\varepsilon_{max} = 64 \times 22 \times 7 \times 10^{-4} = 0.9856\ \text{V}$

The maximum induced current is:
$I_{max} = \dfrac{\varepsilon_{max}}{R}$

$I_{max} = \dfrac{0.9856}{11} = 0.0896\ \text{A}$

$I_{max} = 89.6\ \text{mA} \approx 90\ \text{mA}$

Answer: $90\ \text{mA}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An AC generator having 400 turns and an area of cross section of $2 \times 10^{-3}\ m^2$ rotates with an angular speed of $200\pi\ rad\ s^{-1}$ in a uniform magnetic field of strength 0.4 T. The generator is connected to the primary of an ideal transformer having 500 turns in the primary and 2000 turns in the secondary. The secondary is connected to a $400\ \Omega$ resistive load. What is the rms current in the secondary of the transformer? Assume, the transformer is ideal and the resistance of the coil is negligible
questions.solution:
The peak emf generated by the AC generator is given by $E_0 = NBA\omega$.

Substituting the given values, $E_0 = 400 \times 0.4 \times (2 \times 10^{-3}) \times 200\pi = 64\pi \text{ V}$.

The rms voltage across the primary coil of the transformer is $V_p = \dfrac{E_0}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{64\pi}{\sqrt{2}} \text{ V}$.

For an ideal transformer, the relation between secondary and primary voltages is $\dfrac{V_s}{V_p} = \dfrac{N_s}{N_p}$.

Substituting $N_s = 2000$ and $N_p = 500$, we get $V_s = V_p \times \left( \dfrac{2000}{500} \right) = 4V_p$.

$V_s = 4 \times \dfrac{64\pi}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{256\pi}{\sqrt{2}} \text{ V}$.

The rms current in the secondary circuit is $I_s = \dfrac{V_s}{R}$.

$I_s = \dfrac{\dfrac{256\pi}{\sqrt{2}}}{400} = \dfrac{256\pi}{400\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{0.64\pi}{\sqrt{2}} \text{ A}$.

Using the approximation $\pi \approx 3.14$, we get $0.64\pi \approx 2.01 \approx 2$.

$I_s \approx \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{2}} = \sqrt{2} \text{ A}$.

$I_s \approx 1.41 \text{ A}$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A rectangular loop of resistance $R=5 \Omega$ is placed in a uniform magnetic field such that the magnetic flux through the loop increases according to the relation $\phi=4 t^2-2 t$ where $\phi$ is in weber and $t$ is in second. The current induced at $t=3$ second is:
questions.solution:
The magnetic flux through the loop is given by $\phi = 4t^2 - 2t$.

According to Faraday's law of electromagnetic induction, the induced electromotive force (emf) $\varepsilon$ is given by the negative rate of change of magnetic flux:

$\varepsilon = -\dfrac{d\phi}{dt}$

Differentiating $\phi$ with respect to $t$:

$\dfrac{d\phi}{dt} = \dfrac{d}{dt}(4t^2 - 2t) = 8t - 2$

Thus, the magnitude of the induced emf is $|\varepsilon| = |8t - 2|$.

The induced current $I$ is given by Ohm's law, $I = \dfrac{|\varepsilon|}{R}$, where $R = 5 \Omega$.

At $t = 3$ seconds:

$|\varepsilon| = 8(3) - 2 = 24 - 2 = 22 \text{ V}$

$I = \dfrac{22}{5} = 4.4 \text{ A}$

Answer: 4.4 A

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In an AC generator, a rectangular coil having 400 turns, each having an area of $210 \mathrm{~cm}^2$ is rotated in a uniform magnetic field of magnitude 4 T . If the coil makes 480 revolutions in a minute, the maximum value of emf produced by the generator is:
questions.solution:
The maximum induced emf in an AC generator is given by the formula $\varepsilon_{max} = N A B \omega$, where $N$ is the number of turns, $A$ is the area of the coil, $B$ is the magnetic field strength, and $\omega$ is the angular velocity of the coil.

Given values:
$N = 400$
$A = 210 \text{ cm}^2 = 210 \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^2 = 0.021 \text{ m}^2$
$B = 4 \text{ T}$
Frequency $f = \dfrac{480 \text{ revolutions}}{60 \text{ seconds}} = 8 \text{ Hz}$

The angular velocity $\omega$ is calculated as:
$\omega = 2 \pi f = 2 \times \pi \times 8 = 16 \pi \text{ rad/s}$

Substituting these values into the formula for $\varepsilon_{max}$:
$\varepsilon_{max} = 400 \times 0.021 \times 4 \times 16 \pi$
$\varepsilon_{max} = 33.6 \times 16 \pi$
$\varepsilon_{max} = 537.6 \pi$

Using $\pi \approx 3.14159$:
$\varepsilon_{max} \approx 537.6 \times 3.14159 \approx 1688.93 \approx 1689 \text{ V}$.

Answer: 1689 V

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When current in an inductance is changed at a uniform rate from 15 A to 30 A in 3 s, the self-induced emf in the coil is 25 V. The change in energy of the coil during this process is:
questions.solution:
Rate of change of current: $\dfrac{di}{dt} = \dfrac{30 - 15}{3} = 5$ A/s

Self-induced emf: $e = L\dfrac{di}{dt}$
$25 = L \times 5 \Rightarrow L = 5$ H

Change in energy stored in the inductor:
$\Delta U = \dfrac{1}{2}L(i_f^2 - i_i^2) = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 5 \times (30^2 - 15^2)$

$= 2.5 \times (900 - 225) = 2.5 \times 675 = 1687.5$ J

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A circular coil of area $2 \sqrt{2} \mathrm{~cm}^2$ and resistance $2 \boldsymbol{\Omega}$ is arranged vertically in the east -west direction. A uniform magnetic field 0.2 T is set up across the plane in the north to east direction. Now the magnetic field is removed at a steady rate in 0.4 s What is the current developed in the coil?
questions.solution:
The area of the coil is $A = 2 \sqrt{2} \text{ cm}^2 = 2 \sqrt{2} \times 10^{-4} \text{ m}^2$. The magnetic field $B = 0.2 \text{ T}$ is in the north-east direction, while the coil is in the east-west plane. The normal to the coil points in the north-south direction.

The angle $\theta$ between the magnetic field (north-east) and the normal to the coil (north or south) is $45^{\circ}$.

The initial magnetic flux $\Phi_i$ through the coil is given by $\Phi_i = B A \cos(45^{\circ}) = 0.2 \times (2 \sqrt{2} \times 10^{-4}) \times \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = 0.4 \times 10^{-4} \text{ Wb}$.

The final magnetic flux $\Phi_f$ is $0$ since the magnetic field is removed. The change in flux is $\Delta \Phi = |\Phi_f - \Phi_i| = 0.4 \times 10^{-4} \text{ Wb}$.

The induced electromotive force (emf) is $\varepsilon = \dfrac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t} = \dfrac{0.4 \times 10^{-4}}{0.4} = 10^{-4} \text{ V}$.

The induced current $I$ is given by $I = \dfrac{\varepsilon}{R} = \dfrac{10^{-4}}{2} = 0.5 \times 10^{-4} \text{ A}$.

Answer: $0.5 \times 10^{-4} A$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A current of 2 A is passed through the primary coil. The total flux linked with the secondary coil, which is closely wound over the primary is $2000 \times 10^{-6}$ weber. What is the induced emf in the secondary if the current through the primary increases at a rate of $0.2 \mathrm{As}^{-1}$ ?
questions.solution:
The magnetic flux $\phi$ linked with the secondary coil is proportional to the current $I$ in the primary coil, given by $\phi = MI$, where $M$ is the mutual inductance between the coils.

Given the flux $\phi = 2000 \times 10^{-6} \text{ Wb}$ when the current $I = 2 \text{ A}$, we calculate the mutual inductance $M$ as:

$M = \dfrac{\phi}{I} = \dfrac{2000 \times 10^{-6}}{2} = 1000 \times 10^{-6} \text{ H} = 10^{-3} \text{ H}$

The induced electromotive force (emf) $e$ in the secondary coil is given by Faraday's law of induction, $e = -M \dfrac{dI}{dt}$.

Given the rate of change of current $\dfrac{dI}{dt} = 0.2 \text{ As}^{-1}$, the magnitude of the induced emf is:

$|e| = M \times \dfrac{dI}{dt} = 10^{-3} \times 0.2 = 0.2 \times 10^{-3} \text{ V} = 2 \times 10^{-4} \text{ V}$

Answer: $2 \times 10^{-4} V$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A rectangular coil of 250 turns has an average area of $20 \mathrm{~cm} \times 15 \mathrm{~cm}$. The coil rotates with a speed of 60 cycles per second in a uniform magnetic field of $2 \times 10^{-2} \mathrm{~T}$ about an axis perpendicular to the field. The peak value of the induced emf is:
questions.solution:
The peak value of the induced electromotive force (emf) in a rotating coil is given by the formula $\varepsilon_{0} = N A B \omega$, where $N$ is the number of turns, $A$ is the area of the coil, $B$ is the magnetic field strength, and $\omega$ is the angular velocity.

Given values:
$N = 250$
$A = 20 \text{ cm} \times 15 \text{ cm} = 0.2 \text{ m} \times 0.15 \text{ m} = 0.03 \text{ m}^{2}$
$B = 2 \times 10^{-2} \text{ T}$
Frequency $f = 60 \text{ Hz}$
Angular velocity $\omega = 2 \pi f = 2 \pi \times 60 = 120 \pi \text{ rad/s}$

Substituting these values into the formula:
$\varepsilon_{0} = 250 \times 0.03 \times (2 \times 10^{-2}) \times 120 \pi$

Calculating the product:
$\varepsilon_{0} = 250 \times 0.03 \times 0.02 \times 120 \pi$
$\varepsilon_{0} = 7.5 \times 0.02 \times 120 \pi$
$\varepsilon_{0} = 0.15 \times 120 \pi$
$\varepsilon_{0} = 18 \pi \text{ volt}$

Answer: $18 \pi$ volt

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A long solenoid has 400 turns. When a current of 100 A is passed through it, the resulting magnetic flux linked with each turn of the solenoid is 4 mWb . The self-inductance of the solenoid is
questions.solution:
The self-inductance $L$ of a solenoid is defined by the relation $\Phi_{total} = L I$, where $\Phi_{total}$ is the total magnetic flux linked with all turns of the solenoid.

Given the number of turns $N = 400$, the current $I = 100$ A, and the magnetic flux linked with each turn $\phi = 4$ mWb = $4 \times 10^{-3}$ Wb.

The total magnetic flux linked with the solenoid is $\Phi_{total} = N \phi$.

Substituting the given values:
$\Phi_{total} = 400 \times 4 \times 10^{-3}$ Wb = $1.6$ Wb.

Using the formula $L = \dfrac{\Phi_{total}}{I}$:
$L = \dfrac{1.6 \text{ Wb}}{100 \text{ A}} = 0.016$ H.

Converting to millihenry (mH):
$L = 0.016 \times 1000$ mH = $16$ mH.

Answer: 16 mH

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The magnetic flux $\phi$ through a stationary loop of wire having a resistance R varies with time as $\phi=4 t^2+3 t$. The average emf and total charge flowing in the loop in the time interval $t=0$ to $t=\tau$ respectively are
questions.solution:
The magnetic flux is given by $\phi(t) = 4t^2 + 3t$.

The average induced emf $\varepsilon_{avg}$ in the time interval $t=0$ to $t=\tau$ is defined as the change in flux divided by the time interval:

$\varepsilon_{avg} = -\dfrac{\Delta \phi}{\Delta t} = -\dfrac{\phi(\tau) - \phi(0)}{\tau - 0}$

Substituting the values:

$\phi(\tau) = 4\tau^2 + 3\tau$

$\phi(0) = 4(0)^2 + 3(0) = 0$

$\varepsilon_{avg} = \dfrac{(4\tau^2 + 3\tau) - 0}{\tau} = \dfrac{\tau(4\tau + 3)}{\tau} = 4\tau + 3$

The total charge $q$ flowing through the loop is given by $q = \dfrac{\Delta \phi}{R}$, where $\Delta \phi$ is the magnitude of the change in flux:

$q = \dfrac{|\phi(\tau) - \phi(0)|}{R} = \dfrac{4\tau^2 + 3\tau}{R}$

Answer: $4 \tau+3, \quad \dfrac{4 \tau^2+3 \tau}{R}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In an inductor of self-inductance $2 \mathrm{~mH}$, current changes with time (in sec) according to the relation, $I=(3 t^2-3 t+8) A$. The emf becomes zero at
questions.solution:
The induced electromotive force (emf) in an inductor is given by the formula $\varepsilon = -L \dfrac{dI}{dt}$.

Given $L = 2 \text{ mH} = 2 \times 10^{-3} \text{ H}$ and $I = 3t^2 - 3t + 8$.

Differentiating the current $I$ with respect to time $t$:

$\dfrac{dI}{dt} = \dfrac{d}{dt}(3t^2 - 3t + 8) = 6t - 3$.

The emf becomes zero when $\dfrac{dI}{dt} = 0$.

Setting the derivative to zero:

$6t - 3 = 0$

$6t = 3$

$t = \dfrac{3}{6} = 0.5 \text{ sec}$.

Answer: 0.5 sec

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A wire '$l$' m long bent into a circular loop is placed perpendicular to the magnetic field of flux density $B \text{ Wbm}^{-2}$. Within 0.1sec, the loop is changed into a square of side '$a$' m and flux density is doubled. The value of e.m.f. induced is
questions.solution:
Initial flux: $\Phi_1 = B \cdot \pi r^2 = B \cdot \pi \left(\dfrac{l}{2\pi}\right)^2 = \dfrac{Bl^2}{4\pi}$

Final flux: $\Phi_2 = 2B \cdot a^2 = 2Ba^2$

Induced e.m.f.: $e = -\dfrac{\Delta\Phi}{\Delta t} = -\dfrac{2Ba^2 - \dfrac{Bl^2}{4\pi}}{0.1}$

$e = -10B\left(\dfrac{8\pi a^2 - l^2}{4\pi}\right) = \dfrac{-5B(8\pi a^2 - l^2)}{2\pi}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A metallic rod of length '$a$' is rotated with an angular frequency of $0.2 \mathrm{~rads}^{-1}$ about an axis normal to the rod passing through its one end. A constant and uniform magnetic field of '$\mathrm{B}$' T parallel to the axis exists everywhere. The emf developed across the ends of the rod is
questions.solution:
The motional electromotive force (emf) induced in a rod of length $a$ rotating with angular velocity $\omega$ in a uniform magnetic field $B$ perpendicular to the plane of rotation is given by the integral of $d\epsilon = B v dr$, where $v = \omega r$.

The emf $E$ is calculated as:

$E = \int_{0}^{a} B \omega r dr$

$E = B \omega \left[ \dfrac{r^2}{2} \right]_{0}^{a}$

$E = \dfrac{1}{2} B \omega a^2$

Given the angular frequency $\omega = 0.2 \text{ rad s}^{-1}$, substitute this value into the expression:

$E = \dfrac{1}{2} \times B \times 0.2 \times a^2$

$E = 0.1 \times B \times a^2$

$E = \dfrac{1}{10} B a^2 = \dfrac{B a^2}{10}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\mathrm{Ba}^2}{10}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The current in a coil changes steadily from $3 \mathrm{~A}$ to $5 \mathrm{~A}$ in $0.2 \mathrm{~s}$ when an emf of $2 \mu \mathrm{V}$ is induced in it. The self-inductance of the coil is
questions.solution:
The induced emf $\varepsilon$ in a coil due to a change in current is given by the formula $\varepsilon = L \left| \dfrac{di}{dt} \right|$, where $L$ is the self-inductance of the coil.

Given values are:
Change in current $\Delta i = 5 \text{ A} - 3 \text{ A} = 2 \text{ A}$
Time interval $\Delta t = 0.2 \text{ s}$
Induced emf $\varepsilon = 2 \mu \text{V} = 2 \times 10^{-6} \text{ V}$

The rate of change of current is $\dfrac{di}{dt} = \dfrac{\Delta i}{\Delta t} = \dfrac{2 \text{ A}}{0.2 \text{ s}} = 10 \text{ A/s}$.

Substituting these values into the formula:
$2 \times 10^{-6} \text{ V} = L \times 10 \text{ A/s}$

$L = \dfrac{2 \times 10^{-6}}{10} \text{ H}$

$L = 0.2 \times 10^{-6} \text{ H} = 0.2 \mu \text{H}$.

Answer: 0.2 $\mu H$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A conducting circular loop is placed in a uniform magnetic field $\mathrm{B}=0.125 \mathrm{~T}$ with its plane perpendicular to the loop. If the radius of the loop is made to shrink at a constant rate of $2 \mathrm{~mm} \mathrm{~s}^{-1}$, then the induced emf when the radius is $4 \mathrm{~cm}$ is
questions.solution:
The magnetic flux $\Phi$ through the circular loop is given by $\Phi = B A = B (\pi r^2)$, where $B$ is the magnetic field and $r$ is the radius of the loop.

The induced electromotive force (emf) $\varepsilon$ is given by Faraday's law of induction: $\varepsilon = -\dfrac{d\Phi}{dt}$.

Since $B$ is constant, $\varepsilon = -\dfrac{d}{dt}(B \pi r^2) = -B \pi (2r \dfrac{dr}{dt}) = -2 \pi B r \dfrac{dr}{dt}$.

Given $B = 0.125 \text{ T}$, $r = 4 \text{ cm} = 0.04 \text{ m}$, and the rate of shrinking $\dfrac{dr}{dt} = -2 \text{ mm s}^{-1} = -2 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m s}^{-1}$.

Substituting these values into the expression for magnitude of induced emf:

$|\varepsilon| = 2 \pi (0.125) (0.04) (2 \times 10^{-3})$

$|\varepsilon| = 2 \pi (\dfrac{1}{8}) (4 \times 10^{-2}) (2 \times 10^{-3})$

$|\varepsilon| = 2 \pi (\dfrac{1}{8}) (8 \times 10^{-5}) = 2 \pi \times 10^{-5} \text{ V}$.

Converting to microvolts ($\mu V$):

$|\varepsilon| = 2 \pi \times 10^{-5} \times 10^{6} \mu V = 20 \pi \mu V$.

Answer: $20 \pi \mu V$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The magnetic flux linked with a coil is given by the equation: $\phi = 8t^2 + t + 10$. The e.m.f. induced in the coil at $t = 3$ seconds will be:
questions.solution:
The magnetic flux linked with the coil is given by $\phi = 8t^2 + t + 10$.

The induced electromotive force (e.m.f.) in the coil is given by Faraday's law of induction: $\varepsilon = -\dfrac{d\phi}{dt}$.

Differentiating the flux with respect to time $t$:
$\dfrac{d\phi}{dt} = \dfrac{d}{dt}(8t^2 + t + 10) = 16t + 1$.

The magnitude of the induced e.m.f. is $|\varepsilon| = |-(16t + 1)| = 16t + 1$.

The e.m.f. induced in the $3^{\text{rd}}$ second refers to the instantaneous e.m.f. at $t = 3$ s.

Substituting $t = 3$ into the expression for the magnitude of the e.m.f.:
$|\varepsilon| = 16(3) + 1 = 48 + 1 = 49$ V.

Answer: 49 V

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Select the unit of the coefficient of mutual induction from the following.
questions.solution:
The coefficient of mutual induction $M$ is defined by the relation $\phi = M I$, where $\phi$ is the magnetic flux and $I$ is the current.

From this relation, $M = \dfrac{\phi}{I}$. The unit of magnetic flux $\phi$ is Weber (Wb) and the unit of current $I$ is Ampere (A). Thus, the unit of $M$ is Weber/Ampere.

Alternatively, using Faraday's law of induction, the induced electromotive force $\varepsilon$ is given by $\varepsilon = -M \dfrac{dI}{dt}$.

Rearranging for $M$, we get $M = \dfrac{\varepsilon}{dI/dt}$. The unit of electromotive force $\varepsilon$ is Volt (V), and the unit of $dI/dt$ is Ampere/second (A/s).

Therefore, the unit of $M$ is $\dfrac{\text{Volt}}{\text{Ampere/second}} = \dfrac{\text{Volt} \cdot \text{second}}{\text{Ampere}}$.

Answer: volt. second / ampere

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Around the central part of an air cored solenoid of length $20 \mathrm{~cm}$ and area of cross section $1.4 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~m}^2$ and 3000 turns, another coil of 250 turns is closely wound. A current $2 \mathrm{~A}$ in the solenoid is reversed in $0.2 \mathrm{~s}$, then the induced emf produced is
questions.solution:
The magnetic field $B$ inside a long solenoid is given by $B = \mu_{0} n I$, where $n = \dfrac{N}{l}$ is the number of turns per unit length.

Given: $N_{1} = 3000$, $l = 0.2 \text{ m}$, $I_{initial} = 2 \text{ A}$, $I_{final} = -2 \text{ A}$, $A = 1.4 \times 10^{-3} \text{ m}^2$, $N_{2} = 250$, $\Delta t = 0.2 \text{ s}$.

The magnetic flux $\phi$ through the secondary coil is $\phi = B A = \mu_{0} \left( \dfrac{N_{1}}{l} \right) I A$.

The change in magnetic flux $\Delta \phi$ is $\Delta \phi = \phi_{final} - \phi_{initial} = \mu_{0} \left( \dfrac{N_{1}}{l} \right) A (I_{final} - I_{initial})$.

Substituting the values:
$\Delta \phi = (4 \pi \times 10^{-7}) \times \left( \dfrac{3000}{0.2} \right) \times (1.4 \times 10^{-3}) \times (-2 - 2)$
$\Delta \phi = (4 \pi \times 10^{-7}) \times (15000) \times (1.4 \times 10^{-3}) \times (-4)$
$\Delta \phi = -1.055 \times 10^{-4} \text{ Wb}$ (approx).

The induced emf $\varepsilon$ in the secondary coil is given by Faraday's law: $\varepsilon = -N_{2} \dfrac{\Delta \phi}{\Delta t}$.

$\varepsilon = -250 \times \dfrac{-1.055 \times 10^{-4}}{0.2} = 1250 \times 1.055 \times 10^{-4} = 0.131875 \text{ V}$.

Rounding to the nearest value, $\varepsilon \approx 1.32 \times 10^{-1} \text{ V}$.

Answer: $1.32 \times 10^{-1} \mathrm{~V}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A metallic rod of $2 \mathrm{~m}$ length is rotated with a frequency $100 \mathrm{~Hz}$ about an axis passing through the centre of the circular ring of radius $2 \mathrm{~m}$. A constant magnetic field $2 \mathrm{~T}$ is applied parallel to the axis and perpendicular to the length of the rod. The emf developed across the ends of the rod is :
questions.solution:
The induced emf $e$ across a rod of length $l$ rotating with angular velocity $\omega$ in a uniform magnetic field $B$ perpendicular to the plane of rotation is given by the formula $e = \dfrac{1}{2} B \omega l^2$.

Given parameters are:
Length of the rod $l = 2 \text{ m}$
Frequency $f = 100 \text{ Hz}$
Magnetic field $B = 2 \text{ T}$

The angular velocity $\omega$ is calculated as $\omega = 2 \pi f = 2 \pi \times 100 = 200 \pi \text{ rad/s}$.

Substituting these values into the formula:
$e = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2 \times (200 \pi) \times (2)^2$

$e = 1 \times 200 \pi \times 4$

$e = 800 \pi \text{ V}$.

Answer: 800 $\pi$ volt

questions.q: The magnetic flux linked with a coil satisfies the relation $\phi=\left(4 t^2+6 t+9\right) \mathrm{Wb}$, where $t$ is time in second. The emf induced in the coil at $t=2 \mathrm{~s}$ is
questions.solution:
Given, $\phi=\left(4 t^2+6 t+9\right) \mathrm{Wb}$ and $t=2 \mathrm{~s}$
We know that, $|\varepsilon|=\left|\frac{d \phi}{d t}\right|$
Here, $\left|\frac{d \phi}{d t}\right|=|8 t+6| \Rightarrow\left(\frac{d \phi}{d t}\right)_{t=2}=8 \times 2+6$
Induced emf in the coil $=22 \mathrm{~V}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A metallic rod of $10 \mathrm{~cm}$ is rotated with a frequency 100 revolution per second about an axis perpendicular to its length and passing through its one end in uniform transverse magnetic field of strength $1 \mathrm{~T}$. The emf developed across its ends is:
questions.solution:
The induced electromotive force (emf) across the ends of a conducting rod of length $l$ rotating with angular velocity $\omega$ in a uniform magnetic field $B$ perpendicular to the plane of rotation is given by the formula:

$\varepsilon = \dfrac{1}{2} B \omega l^2$

Given values are:
Length $l = 10 \text{ cm} = 0.1 \text{ m}$
Frequency $f = 100 \text{ rev/s}$
Magnetic field $B = 1 \text{ T}$

The angular velocity $\omega$ is related to frequency $f$ by:
$\omega = 2 \pi f = 2 \times \pi \times 100 = 200 \pi \text{ rad/s}$

Substituting these values into the emf formula:
$\varepsilon = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 1 \times (200 \pi) \times (0.1)^2$

$\varepsilon = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 200 \pi \times 0.01$

$\varepsilon = 100 \pi \times 0.01$

$\varepsilon = \pi \text{ V}$

Using $\pi \approx 3.14$, we get:
$\varepsilon = 3.14 \text{ V}$

Answer: 3.14 V

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: One volt induced emf is produced in the secondary coil when the current through the primary coil is changed from $3 \mathrm{~A}$ to $1 \mathrm{~A}$ in 100 milliseconds. the mutual inductance of the two coil is:
questions.solution:
The induced emf $\varepsilon$ in the secondary coil is given by the formula $\varepsilon = -M \dfrac{dI}{dt}$, where $M$ is the mutual inductance and $\dfrac{dI}{dt}$ is the rate of change of current in the primary coil.

Given values are:
$\varepsilon = 1 \text{ V}$
Change in current $\Delta I = 1 \text{ A} - 3 \text{ A} = -2 \text{ A}$
Time interval $\Delta t = 100 \text{ ms} = 0.1 \text{ s}$

The magnitude of the induced emf is $|\varepsilon| = M \left| \dfrac{\Delta I}{\Delta t} \right|$.

Substituting the values:
$1 = M \times \left| \dfrac{-2}{0.1} \right|$
$1 = M \times 20$
$M = \dfrac{1}{20} \text{ H}$
$M = 0.05 \text{ H}$

Answer: 0.05 H

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The magnetic flux linked with a coil satisfies the relation $\phi=\left(4 t^2+6 t+9\right) \mathrm{Wb}$, where $t$ is time in second. The emf induced in the coil at $t=2 \mathrm{~s}$ is
questions.solution:
The induced electromotive force (emf) in a coil is given by Faraday's law of induction, which states that the magnitude of the induced emf is equal to the rate of change of magnetic flux through the coil:

$|\varepsilon| = \left| \dfrac{d\phi}{dt} \right|$

Given the magnetic flux $\phi = 4t^2 + 6t + 9$, we differentiate this expression with respect to time $t$:

$\dfrac{d\phi}{dt} = \dfrac{d}{dt}(4t^2 + 6t + 9)$

$\dfrac{d\phi}{dt} = 8t + 6$

To find the induced emf at $t = 2$ s, we substitute $t = 2$ into the expression for the rate of change of flux:

$\varepsilon = 8(2) + 6$

$\varepsilon = 16 + 6 = 22 \text{ V}$

Answer: 22 V

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A constant current flows from $A$ to $B$ as shown in the figure. What is the direction of current in the circle?
questions.solution:
The problem describes a straight wire carrying a constant current from A to B. A circular loop is placed in the vicinity of this wire. According to the principle of electromagnetic induction, a current is induced in a closed loop only if there is a change in the magnetic flux linked with the loop. Since the current in the wire is constant, the magnetic field produced by it is also constant. Consequently, the magnetic flux through the circular loop remains constant over time. By Faraday's law of induction, the induced electromotive force is given by $\varepsilon = -\dfrac{d\phi}{dt}$. Since the magnetic flux $\phi$ is constant, $\dfrac{d\phi}{dt} = 0$, which implies that the induced electromotive force is zero. Therefore, no current is induced in the circle.

Answer: None of the above

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A magnet $N S$ is suspended from a spring and while it oscillates, the magnet moves in and out of the coil $C$. The coil is connected to a galvanometer $G$. Then, as the magnet oscillates,
options: $G$ shows deflection to the left and right with constant amplitude
G shows deflection to the left and right but the amplitude steadily decreases
questions.solution:
The magnet is attached to the spring. This magnet will execute simple harmonic motion. When a coil is placed in such a way that magnet moves in and out of the coil, an emf is induced in the coil which opposes the movement of magnet in the coil. Due to this induced emf galvanometer will show deflections to the left and right periodically.

As the emf is induced in the coil eddy currents are also induced in the magnet, which lowers down the total magnetic strength of the magnet. Due to this reason, the magnetic flux linked with the coil decrease and hence amplitude of the deflections produced in the galvanometer also decreases.

questions.q: The normal magnetic flux passing through a coil changes with time according to the equation $\phi=6 t^{2}-5 t+1$. What is the magnitude of the induced current at $t=0.253 \mathrm{~s}$ and resistance $10 \Omega$ ?
questions.solution:
Given, magnetic flux

\phi=6 t^{2}-5 t+1, R=10 \Omega

Induced emf,
$e=-\frac{d \phi}{d t}=-\frac{d}{d t}\left(6 t^{2}-5 t+1\right)e=-12 t+5$
At $t=0.253 \mathrm{~s}, e=-12 \times 0.253+5=-3.036+5=1.964 \mathrm{~V}\therefore$ Induced current, $I=\frac{e}{R}=\frac{1.964}{10}=0.1964 \mathrm{~A} \simeq 0.2 \mathrm{~A}$

electric flux linked with the coil changes
